featured_reviews.name: Tejaswini Hulsurkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Panshikar is a well-known Maharashtrian food joint in Vile Parle, Mumbai. It serves tasty, simple, and homely food that reminds you of traditional home cooking. The place is clean, comfortable, and always full of customers.

Their Misal Pav, Thalipeeth, Pithla Bhakri, and Puran Poli are some of the most popular dishes. Each item is fresh, flavorful. The modaks and sweets here are perfect for anyone with a sweet tooth.

The staff is friendly, and the service is quick. Even when it’s crowded, the food quality stays the same every time. Prices are reasonable, and portions are just right.

This is not a fancy restaurant, but it has a warm and homely feel that makes you want to come back. It’s a great place for breakfast, lunch, or an evening snack with friends and family. If you want to enjoy real Maharashtrian food in Mumbai, Panshikar is one of the best choices. Do not forget to grab some packaged snacks home. Must visit place.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
Panshikar in Vile Parle East is a well-known and highly trusted name when it comes to authentic Maharashtrian food. If you enjoy traditional flavours, this place rarely disappoints. Their Sabudana Wada is excellent—crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and perfectly spiced. The Thalipith is another highlight, served fresh and full of flavour. The Misal is also superb, with a balanced spice level and a taste that truly feels homemade. The food overall has a comforting, authentic appeal that keeps customers coming back.

The outlet remains quite busy, especially on weekend mornings, which is a testament to its popularity among locals and visitors alike. Despite the rush, the hygiene levels are good, and the staff works efficiently to manage orders and customers. They also offer delivery through Zomato and Swiggy, which is convenient for those who want to enjoy their dishes at home without waiting.

However, there are a few practical limitations. The seating is limited, and space can feel a bit tight during peak hours. There is no air-conditioning, so summers may not be the most comfortable time to dine in. Parking is also a challenge, like many places in this area, so planning ahead helps.

Still, the quality and authenticity of the food make it absolutely worth visiting. If you are a fan of Maharashtrian cuisine or looking to try some traditional dishes made right, Panshikar remains one of the best and most reliable places in Vile Parle East.

featured_reviews.name: ShanuKumar Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Strolling down Rani Sati Marg in Malad East, I spotted the modest yet inviting storefront of Ajay Mishtan tucked into Dwarkesh Building. Despite its small space—just seating for a handful—I felt its welcoming charm the moment I stepped inside  .

The display case was brimming with colorful sweets and snacks: golden samosas, crisp fafda, pillowy jalebis glistening in syrup. I couldn’t resist ordering a warm samosa and a couple of gulab jamuns. The samosa was delightfully crisp and savory—comfort food perfection—while the jalebis were light, sweet, and just chewy enough to bring a broad smile to my face.

I grabbed a seat on a small bench. The shop’s friendly owner nodded a greeting, and the casual chatter around—regulars sharing neighborhood news—immediately made me feel at home. There was a real sense of community in the air.

A few folks waited patiently to order, while others tapped away at their phones, eagerly anticipating takeaway boxes. I noticed how the shop balanced being a quick grab-and-go spot with a cozy breakfast corner.

With each bite, I appreciated not just the flavors but the story: the shop’s reputation for generous portion sizes yet budget-friendly pricing—about ₹200 for two, according to locals  . It felt like a place built for everyday joy, not flashy acclaim.

Leaving Ajay Mishtan, I felt satisfied—and a little nostalgic. There’s something magical about simple places like this: the crunch of a freshly fried snack, the syrupy sweetness of jalebi, and the genuine warmth of a neighborhood gem. It reminded me that happiness can often be found in the little, routine moments—especially when shared over delicious food in familiar company.
